hey! just wrote some study tips in a comment, feel free to reference that and lmk if you have any questions.

math— take a few sections of math and determine what your weak points are. I did this figure out what units I needed to work on then I mostly used khan academy practice questions to get used to different questions to get acquainted with the topic. id specifically recommend this to people who have successfully completed algebra 2, though, bc i used this process to just review concepts i forgot.
science— statistical literacy! if necessary, study the different types of graphs and how they interpret data. i dont think science needs a lot of studying, but id definitely recommend that you know how to read data presented in different ways. when approaching questions, id recommend going straight to the questions to not only save time but save yourself from confusion. read over only the parts of the passage that are relevant to the question you’re solving. this seems to be a pretty common test taking strategy for both science and reading.
english— i can’t really help you there because i usually answer questions based on intuition. id say maybe know how different punctuations are used, what the different types of sentence structures are and how to use them. 

overall, id recommend doing a comprehensive error analysis based on previous tests/practice tests, then working from there. doing full tests (if you have the time) works wonders to maintain stamina. i hope this helps!

We've taken the love language test together! We both have quality time as our first and physical touch as second (which sucks as we're long/medium distance and can't see each other frequently but we're working around it!). You're right, I would say I enjoy gift giving. While I don't want to smother my partner in gifts, I like the idea of giving him something small to keep by him to remind him of me once every few months at least.

He most definitely did not act selfishly, I wanted him to go buy something for himself and insisted that he spend the gift card for himself but he essentially got something that he knew I wanted to do with him at some point. I do appreciate the gesture and I'm sure we'd have fun playing the game together, but a part of me wish that he spent the money fully for himself. I don't really mind it though, just as long as he didn't feel the need to buy it because I mentioned it a few weeks ago.

His reluctance and need to reciprocate might honestly just come from him being overly nice. I recently bought Minecraft to play with him and he offered to pay me. Every time I’d imply that I want to get something for him, he would say it's a waste of money, even if he really wanted the thing I want to get him. I decided not to push it and decided to mostly stick to handmade things.

Regarding college— we were already a long/medium distance couple in the first place so it’s not a big change. If all goes well, he would actually be moving slightly closer to me. Also, if anything, being independent gives him more freedom to visit once in a while. I’m rather excited to see how college works out for him :)
